reviews.one_line_contribution: Transfer across tasks a hierarchical prior over two nuisance statistics of reflective prompt search - rho, the base rate at which an LLM-proposed edit is a true improvement, and the distribution of improvement magnitudes - and use it as the starting belief of a spike-and-slab sequential accept/reject test that replaces GEPA's fixed-minibatch candidate evaluation, leaving proposal and Pareto selection untouched.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two literatures jointly cover the two halves of the method. (1) Best-arm-identification / racing for prompt selection: TRIPLE (Shi et al., 2024, 'Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification') already replaces fixed-budget prompt scoring with adaptive sequential allocation under a rollout budget, and irace / Hoeffding races / Successive Halving do the same in the general configuration-search setting. The proposal's own arm (iii), uninformative racing, concedes this half. (2) Prior-guided and transfer Bayesian optimization: piBO (Hvarfner et al., 2022) injects a user/meta prior into the acquisition function, and RGPE-style ranking-weighted transfer surrogates (Feurer et al.) pool source-task statistics into a target-task prior; meta-learned racing and meta-learned early stopping in AutoML transfer exactly 'how noisy and how rewarding is a proposal here' rather than the search space. The proposal's Related Work dismisses meta-BO on the grounds that it 'requires a shared, low-dimensional, parametric search space', but that objection does not apply to the object actually transferred here - a prior over (rho, effect size) is a two-to-three parameter surrogate-free prior, which is precisely the regime where transferring prior beliefs about outcome statistics rather than the domain is standard. The efficient-LLM-evaluation line (tinyBenchmarks, Anchor Points, IRT-based adaptive evaluation) is a third threat: it transfers item- and candidate-level statistics across tasks specifically to cut evaluation cost, which is the same conceptual move. What is left as novel is the framing sentence ('the search space does not transfer, the noise model does') plus its measurement on GEPA-style runs, which is a positioning delta, not a mechanism.
reviews.strongest_objection: The proposal is caught in a dilemma its own risk section (1) half-admits, and no arm in the plan escapes it. The transferred object is two scalars and a shape. Either rho and the effect scale are stable across domains - in which case a hand-set constant prior reproduces TAP and the entire source-harvesting apparatus (6 tasks x 300 rollouts x 3 seeds x 400-example probe scoring of every candidate) buys nothing - or they are task-idiosyncratic, in which case the pooled prior is refuted by Experiment 2. The band in which a *pooled hierarchical* prior beats both a fixed sensible prior and cheap online estimation is narrow, and the proposal's own Falsifiable Prediction (c) shrinks it to roughly rollouts 1-60. Worse, the headline number is arithmetically implausible: a prior over a Bernoulli rate is worth some small effective number of pseudo-observations (at most a handful of candidates, given that between-task heterogeneity across only six source tasks will inflate the pooled variance), yet Prediction (b) claims 2-5 test points over cold-start GEPA at 50 rollouts. Almost all of any such gain must come from adaptivity, not transfer - and adaptivity is arm (iii), uninformative racing, which the proposal itself flags as 'the baseline most likely to erase the contribution'. That leaves the transfer-specific claim as the 1-3 point margin over uninformative racing in Prediction (b), a margin that is very likely inside the treatment-free null-replicate floor that Experiment 1 is designed to establish (the track brief reports that a null replicate reproduced the apparent gain of the best real treatment). Under the proposal's own stated decision rule - 'any effect below the treatment-free null-replicate floor is reported as null regardless of p-value' - the central claim of the paper is then reported as null by construction. Three secondary defects compound this. (a) The power claim is pseudoreplicated: 6 targets x 5 seeds is treated as n=30 paired observations detecting 1.5 points at 80% power, but the unit of generalization for a domain-transfer claim is the task, so the effective n is 6 and the mixed model's task random effect will not rescue a 1-3 point cross-domain claim. Symmetrically, the ICC and leave-one-task-out predictive likelihood in Experiment 2 - billed as the measurement that 'decides the hypothesis independent of downstream gains' - estimate a between-group variance component from six groups, which yields an interval covering nearly the whole [0,1] range and cannot decide anything. (b) The 'strictly paired design' in which the reflection proposal stream is 'replayed identically across evaluation-policy conditions' is impossible past the first divergent accept/reject decision: TAP and cold-start GEPA then hold different Pareto pools, so different parents, so different reflections. The hedge 'where possible' is doing load-bearing work for a variance-reduction claim that expires after roughly one candidate. (c) rho is defined as P(delta>0) with no minimum meaningful delta, estimated against 400-example probe deltas. Near delta=0, where most reflective edits actually live, the sign is dominated by probe noise, so measured rho is biased toward 0.5 and its cross-task stability is partly an artifact of that shrinkage - i.e., the paper could 'confirm' low ICC for measurement reasons. Finally, rho is strongly non-stationary *within* a run (later candidates face a stronger parent, so improvement rates decay); a static per-task scalar ignores the largest variance component, and an online estimator tracks it while the transferred prior cannot, which independently predicts arm (iv) wins.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes would make this reviewable as a main-track contribution. (1) Add the two omitted baselines below and pre-commit that if a hand-set constant prior matches TAP, the paper reports 'no transfer occurred'. (2) Make the transferred object non-trivial: condition rho and the effect-size slab on iteration index and parent validation score (and, ideally, on a cheap task-similarity feature so that transfer can be *predicted* before it is paid for, which is the open question the track brief actually poses). A prior over a decay curve is something an online estimator with 15 candidates genuinely cannot recover; a prior over a single scalar is not. (3) Fix the statistics: state the minimum meaningful delta in the definition of rho and deconvolve probe-set noise from the estimated effect-size distribution; power the between-task variance claim with roughly 20+ source clusters rather than 6, and report ICC with a confidence interval; drop the identical-replay claim or restrict pairing to the pre-divergence prefix; and do the primary power calculation at the task level (n=6), reporting the honest MDE, which will likely show that the 1-3 point transfer-vs-racing gap is not detectable as designed. (4) Derive, before running anything, the effective sample size of the transferred prior in candidate-evaluations, and pre-register the maximum gain that quantity can support; if that ceiling is below the null-replicate floor, the experiment should not be run as the headline claim and should instead be framed as the measurement paper that Experiment 2 already is. Also: actually perform a recent-preprint search and populate the empty collision check.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two, both cheap and both potentially fatal. (1) A hand-set constant prior - the same sequential spike-and-slab test with rho and the slab fixed a priori to plausible values (say rho = 0.2-0.3 with a moderate effect scale) and no source harvesting at all. This is the arm that isolates whether anything was *transferred* as opposed to merely *assumed*; the plan's flat-prior racing arm (iii) does not cover it, because a flat prior is not the same as a sensible fixed prior, and the proposal's own Risk Factor (1) concedes the contribution collapses if this arm ties. (2) Cold-start GEPA with a swept minibatch size at matched rollouts. GEPA's fixed minibatch is a hyperparameter, and mechanism (5b), 'more candidates proposed per budget', is obtainable simply by shrinking it from 5 to 2. No reviewer will credit a Bayesian sequential test over a fixed-minibatch baseline whose single relevant hyperparameter was left at its default. A third, weaker omission: no arm reports the reflection-call cost separately, so the token-axis comparison will conflate executor rollouts with frontier reflector spend, and TAP's extra candidates per budget consume more reflector calls than cold-start at the same rollout count.
reviews.preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and Related Work opens with '(All citations unverified; literature search was unavailable.)'. By the standard applied here this is a weakness, not a neutral: the proposal's central novelty claim is a negative one - 'a conceptual dissociation none of these make' - and a negative claim over a literature nobody searched is unsupported. This is also the worst possible area in which to skip the search. Adaptive/budget-aware evaluation for GEPA- and MIPRO-style optimizers is exactly the kind of incremental efficiency result that appears on arXiv monthly, and GEPA itself is a 2025 preprint whose follow-ups (adaptive minibatching, early-stopping candidate evaluation, bandit-based candidate selection, budget-aware Pareto maintenance) are the most likely scoop. Named candidates the authors must clear before claiming novelty, from memory and therefore themselves unverified: TRIPLE (Shi et al., 2024) for best-arm-identification prompt selection under a fixed budget; piBO (Hvarfner et al., 2022) and RGPE-style transfer surrogates for injecting meta-learned priors into sequential search; irace and Successive Halving for racing with priors; tinyBenchmarks / Anchor Points / IRT-based adaptive LLM evaluation (2024) for transferring evaluation statistics across tasks to cut scoring cost. If any 2025-2026 preprint has already put an informative, cross-task prior into GEPA's minibatch decision - a very natural thing to try - this proposal's mechanism is gone and only the ICC measurement survives. As submitted, novelty is asserted, not established.

reviews.one_line_contribution: Rather than transferring prompts, skeletons, or reflection heuristics across tasks, transfer a hierarchical prior over the *nuisance statistics of the search itself* — rho, the base rate at which a reflection-proposed edit is a true improvement, and the effect-size distribution of those improvements — and use it as the starting belief of a spike-and-slab sequential accept/reject test that replaces GEPA's fixed-size minibatch candidate evaluation, leaving proposal and selection untouched.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two bodies of work jointly enclose the contribution. (1) Adaptive evaluation allocation for prompt selection is already established: TRIPLE (Shi et al., 'Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification', NeurIPS 2024) casts prompt evaluation under a fixed budget as best-arm identification and gets exactly the 'stop wasting rollouts on doomed candidates' win the proposal's mechanism (5a) claims as its own; the proposal's Related Work cites racing/SH/Hyperband generically but never engages BAI-for-prompts, which is the nearest neighbour in its own subfield. (2) Injecting an *informative, transferred* prior into a racing/allocation procedure is the core of prior-informed and meta-learned HPO: piBO (Hvarfner et al., ICLR 2022), BOPrO (Souza et al., 2021), PriorBand (Mallik et al., NeurIPS 2023) — which is precisely successive-halving-with-a-prior — and transfer surrogates such as RGPE (Feurer et al.). The proposal pre-empts this by saying transfer BO 'requires a shared, low-dimensional, parametric search space,' but that is a rebuttal to transferring a *surrogate over the search space*, not to PriorBand-style transfer of allocation beliefs, which needs no shared parameterization either. What genuinely remains is narrow: the prior is over the noise/improvement model rather than over the optimum, and it is fit hierarchically across source tasks. That is a real but modest delta, and the proposal's own baseline (iii) exists to measure exactly how thin the sliver is.
reviews.strongest_objection: Nothing in the design separates the claimed gain from 'GEPA's default minibatch size is simply too large.' Prediction (b) — 2-5 test points over cold-start GEPA at 50 rollouts, with >=60% of it traced (prediction e) to rollouts saved on rejected candidates — is the signature of spending fewer examples per candidate, which any practitioner obtains by lowering one integer. Cold-start GEPA is run only at 'its default fixed minibatch'; the ablation grid varies tau_a/tau_r, block size, and per-candidate cap for TAP but never sweeps the competitor's single most important allocation hyperparameter. A reviewer will read arm (i) as a strawman and ask what survives against GEPA with minibatch tuned once on the source tasks — a transfer of one scalar with no hierarchy, no spike-and-slab, and no sequential test. Second, the variance argument that licenses the whole statistical plan is overstated: 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed identically across evaluation-policy conditions' is impossible past the first accept/reject decision in GEPA, because the parent chosen for the next mutation depends on which candidates entered the Pareto pool. The qualifier 'where possible' quietly concedes this. Without a genuinely paired proposal stream, the effective per-comparison SD reverts toward the measured per-run ~3 points, and the '1.5-point paired difference at 80% power with n=30' calculation — the design's answer to the brief's failure mode #2 — is not supported. Third, rho is treated as a task-level constant, but it is manifestly non-stationary within a run (edits to a weak initial prompt succeed far more often than edits near convergence) and also depends on the reflector model and parent quality. Experiment 2 reports between-task vs within-task (across-seed) ICC and never conditions on iteration index, so the study can find 'rho transfers across tasks' while the real structure is 'rho is a decreasing function of optimization stage' — under which the online-prior baseline (iv), which sees the current stage, should dominate TAP everywhere except the first few candidates.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (a) Add the minibatch/stop-rule sweep for cold-start GEPA and MIPROv2, and report TAP against the best-tuned competitor, not the default one; if TAP's advantage is only over an untuned baseline, say so and reframe the paper as a measurement paper. (b) Add a source-free generic prior arm (see missing_baseline) so 'transfer' is isolated from 'having any informative prior at all.' (c) Drop or heavily qualify the 'strictly paired design that removes proposal randomness' claim, state explicitly at which candidate index the streams must diverge, and redo the power calculation using the empirically measured paired correlation from the step-1 seed-replicate runs rather than an assumed one; alternatively run a genuinely paired sub-study in which the candidate sequence is frozen offline and only the allocation policy varies, and report that as the mechanism experiment while the full runs carry the end-to-end claim. (d) Model rho as stage-dependent (e.g., rho indexed by iteration or by parent validation score) and report the ICC decomposition with iteration as a third variance component; a hierarchical prior that pools across tasks but ignores within-run drift is the wrong object if drift dominates. (e) Resolve the internal inconsistency between 'Pareto selection exactly as is' and an accept test on aggregate P(delta>0): GEPA accepts on per-instance Pareto dominance, so the proposed test changes the selection semantics, not just the budget allocation. (f) Cut scope to fit the brief's stated ceiling of a few dozen optimization runs (see feasibility), and pre-register which of experiments 5-7 are contingent on the main result. (g) Do the preprint search and write the collision check.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two, either of which could erase the contribution. First and most damaging: cold-start GEPA/MIPROv2 with the minibatch size and promotion rule tuned on the source tasks and carried over — a 'transfer one integer' baseline that requires none of TAP's machinery and directly targets mechanism (5a). Second: a source-free generic prior — a hand-set rho (say 0.25) and a generic slab plugged into the identical sequential test, with no hierarchical fitting and no source runs at all. The proposal names this outcome in Risk Factor (1) as the scenario where 'the contribution becomes use a sensible fixed prior,' yet never instruments it: the ablations contrast single-source vs six-source pooling but never drop source-fitting entirely, so the experiment that would trigger the paper's own stated deflation is the one arm not run. Note that the uninformative-racing baseline (iii) does not substitute — a flat prior is not the same as a well-chosen fixed prior, and it is the well-chosen fixed prior that costs nothing.
reviews.preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and Related Work opens with '(All citations unverified; literature search was unavailable.)' By the standard stated in the review instructions this is a substantive weakness, not a neutral: the proposal asserts a 'conceptual dissociation none of these make' about a literature it has not read, and even its anchor citations (GEPA, MIPROv2) are self-declared unverified. The exposure is high rather than theoretical, because GEPA is itself a 2025 artifact and budget-aware / adaptive-evaluation variants of reflective prompt optimizers are exactly the fast-moving corner where 2025-2026 preprints cluster; 'sample-efficient candidate evaluation for DSPy/GEPA-style optimizers' and 'meta-learned priors for LLM optimizer budget allocation' are near-certain preprint topics in that window. I cannot from memory name a preprint that makes this exact claim (transferring the noise model rather than the artifact), and I am not able to search here — but the already-published TRIPLE (NeurIPS 2024) covers the adaptive-allocation half and PriorBand (NeurIPS 2023) covers the informative-prior-into-racing half, so the burden is entirely on the authors to show the intersection is open. A resubmission must include a dated search over arXiv cs.CL/cs.LG for the last ~6 months on 'prompt optimization budget allocation', 'GEPA sample efficiency', 'best-arm identification prompt', and 'transfer prior racing', with the queries and dates reported.

reviews.one_line_contribution: Instead of transferring prompt text or reflection heuristics across tasks, harvest from source runs a two-parameter 'noise model' of the search — rho, the base rate at which reflection-proposed edits are true improvements, and the distribution of improvement magnitudes — and inject it as the starting belief of a spike-and-slab sequential accept/reject test that replaces GEPA's fixed-minibatch candidate evaluation, with the claim scoped as a small-budget-only Pareto gain plus an ICC measurement of how task-invariant those statistics actually are.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Three literatures jointly cover the two halves and are not engaged. (1) For the adaptive-allocation half: best-arm-identification / bandit selection of prompt candidates under a fixed evaluation budget (Shi et al., 'Efficient Prompt Optimization Through the Lens of Best Arm Identification', TRIPLE, 2024) already replaces fixed-minibatch scoring with sequential elimination in exactly this setting; the Related Work names Hoeffding races, irace and Successive Halving generically but never the prompt-optimization instantiation, which is the one a reviewer will name first. (2) For the informative-prior half: prior-guided BO (piBO/BOPrO) and meta-BO transfer surrogates (RGPE) transfer a belief about where improvement lives; the proposal dismisses these as needing a shared parametric search space, but that objection does not apply to what TAP actually transfers — a prior over the improvement variable, not over the search space, which is precisely what piBO-style methods place. (3) Most damaging: empirical-Bayes sequential testing in industrial A/B platforms fits a prior over the win base rate and the lift distribution from a corpus of past experiments and uses it to stop tests early (Deng et al., 'Continuous monitoring of A/B tests without pain', 2016, and the fat-tailed-lift literature). 'Fit a prior over (base rate of true wins, effect sizes) from historical experiments, then run sequential accept/reject' is that method verbatim; running the experiments inside GEPA rather than a web product is the domain swap the track brief explicitly says reviewers score as a modest delta. Also, the cold-start competitor is described as pure fixed-minibatch evaluation, but GEPA as published already gates on a minibatch and only then spends full validation, i.e. it already implements a crude two-stage screen — the strawman version of the main baseline weakens the novelty claim further.
reviews.strongest_objection: The only comparison that establishes the contribution is underpowered by the proposal's own numbers, and the variance reduction that the power analysis depends on is unobtainable. Baseline (iii), uninformative racing, isolates transfer from adaptivity, and baseline (iv), the online prior fit on the target's first K=15 candidates, isolates transfer from cheap local estimation. Prediction (b) puts TAP over racing at 1-3 test points and prediction (c) confines the win over the online prior to the first 40-60 rollouts, while Measurement and Noise Control states an MDE of 1.5 points at n=30 paired — so the decisive contrast sits at or below the detection threshold, which is failure mode 2 in the track brief. That MDE is itself optimistic: it rests on 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed identically across evaluation-policy conditions', but in a reflective optimizer the next proposal is conditioned on the current parent and its traces, so the moment two arms make different accept decisions — the first candidate, by construction, since that is the treatment — the streams diverge and cannot be replayed. Pairing is therefore trajectory-level, not proposal-level, and the true paired SD is closer to the ~3-point per-run test SD than the design assumes. Compounding this, risk factor (6) caps reflection at ~30 calls per run, so the online-prior baseline with K=15 warms up halfway through every run; TAP's exclusive advantage window is at most 15 candidates in a 30-candidate run, and any result in that window is a handful of accept/reject decisions per seed. A reviewer will conclude the paper is powered for the comparison it must win (cold-start GEPA) and not for the two that decide whether 'transfer' is the mechanism at all.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Make Experiment 2 the paper and fix its statistics. (a) Six source tasks gives an ICC estimated from six clusters, whose confidence interval spans nearly the whole range; no power analysis is offered for the measurement the proposal calls decisive. Expand to 20+ task clusters, or report the ICC interval and accept that the measurement can only be descriptive. (b) rho is nonstationary within a run — it falls as the parent improves — so fitting one rho per task pools early-run and late-run candidates, inflating within-task variance and deflating the between-task ICC. As written, the central test is biased toward confirming the hypothesis, and a pooled prior can pass it while being miscalibrated at every actual search depth. Condition rho and the slab on search depth or parent quality and report the ICC at matched depth. (c) Effect sizes in raw accuracy points are not commensurable across 2WikiMultiHop F1, GSM8K exact match, MBPP pass@1 and an LLM-judged instruction set with different base rates and ceilings; normalize the slab to per-example SD units before any claim that 'three numbers' port across domains. (d) Experiment 5c measures precision of accept decisions but never recall: under a low-rho spike prior the test's failure mode is fast rejection of the rare true improvement that the evolutionary search depends on, so report the false-reject rate against probe-set ground truth and show TAP does not simply become 'reject everything faster' with progress bounded by the per-candidate cap. (e) Either power the TAP-vs-racing and TAP-vs-online contrasts directly (more seeds or more targets at the 25/50 checkpoints only) or drop the point predictions in (b) and (c) and report curves with intervals. (f) Prediction (b) demands a crossover CI narrower than the checkpoint spacing while the predicted crossover, 100-250 rollouts, already spans three checkpoints (100/200/300); zero-crossing statistics bootstrap very wide, and this prediction should be replaced by a directly measurable one. (g) Run and report an actual preprint search.
reviews.missing_baseline: A fixed-minibatch-size sweep on cold-start GEPA. The mechanism decomposition predicts that >=60% of TAP's gain comes from spending fewer rollouts per rejected candidate (5a), but simply halving or tuning the fixed minibatch size — one hyperparameter, no transfer, no adaptivity, no source runs — buys the same trade of examples-per-candidate for candidates-per-budget, and at 25-50 rollouts it is the arm most likely to match TAP. Without it the headline gain is not attributable to the transferred prior. A second, nearly as damaging omission is a generic hand-set prior arm (e.g. rho fixed at some plausible value with an off-the-shelf slab, no source harvesting at all): risk factor (1) concedes this is a live outcome — 'the contribution becomes use a sensible fixed prior' — yet it appears nowhere in the arm list, so the experiment cannot distinguish 'the harvested cross-task prior' from 'any reasonable prior'. The oracle-fit and online-fit arms bracket TAP from above and below but neither substitutes for this one.
reviews.preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and Related Work opens by conceding 'All citations unverified; literature search was unavailable.' No search was performed, so the novelty claim is unestablished rather than merely unproven — under the track's own instruction that counts as a weakness, and it is the main reason novelty is scored at 4 rather than 6. The proposal is also unusually exposed here because its neighbourhood is one where fast-moving 2024-2025 work sits directly on the mechanism: bandit / best-arm-identification allocation of evaluation budget over prompt candidates (TRIPLE, 2024) and the wave of budget-aware and early-stopping variants of GEPA/DSPy candidate evaluation that followed GEPA's 2025 release. Any of these could already contain the sequential accept/reject half; an informative empirical-Bayes prior over (win rate, effect size) fitted from prior runs is the only remaining delta, and it is a well-established technique in sequential A/B testing. At minimum, targeted searches for 'prompt optimization bandit budget allocation', 'GEPA sample efficiency early stopping', 'meta-learned prior sequential testing hyperparameter', and 'transfer prompt optimization search policy' must be run and reported before novelty can be scored above borderline.
